items.q: Does GoHighLevel have a real estate template?
items.a:
Yes. HighLevel publishes a Real Estate Agent Snapshot, a template you install into a sub-account, and the FAQ on its pricing page names real estate among the industries in its Snapshot library. HighLevel's help article says the template supplies a website, forms, calendars, workflows, email campaigns, online ads and social posts for capturing and nurturing leads.

That article was last updated in May 2024, so plan to rewrite the copy, test every workflow and make sure your forms collect the texting consent that A2P registration asks about before anything goes out. Its listed contents include no contacts or property listings, so leads and listings still have to come from you. On the $97 Starter plan, the template is installed in one of the 3 sub-accounts the plan includes, and every text, call and email its workflows send is billed from the wallet at the usual rates.

items.q: Can GoHighLevel show MLS listings on an agent's website?
items.a:
Not through any feature HighLevel describes. According to HighLevel's real estate page, GoHighLevel's website and funnel builder can publish listing pages you build yourself, property funnels, home valuation campaigns and open house sign-up pages, but neither that page nor HighLevel's pricing page describes an MLS feed or IDX home search among GoHighLevel's features. A request for an IDX integration on HighLevel's public ideas board, first posted in May 2020, still read 'Under review' on 6 October 2026, and comments beneath it point users to third-party IDX services.

Follow Up Boss does not host listings either; its FAQ says it is not a website company. It connects to IDX websites run by other providers, and its pixel on an IDX site records which properties each lead viewed. With either CRM, MLS search on an agent's site comes from a separate IDX provider.

items.q: Is Follow Up Boss cheaper than GoHighLevel for a real estate team?
items.a:
Only for a single agent, if you compare subscriptions. On 6 October 2026, Follow Up Boss's Grow plan cost $69 per user a month on monthly billing, below GoHighLevel's $97 Starter plan, but from the second agent on, Grow costs more than Starter, which includes unlimited users.

GoHighLevel then adds metered usage that Follow Up Boss mostly does not: $0.00747 per text segment plus a carrier fee, per-minute calls, and A2P registration at $22.50 once plus a monthly campaign fee. Follow Up Boss covers its customers' registration fees and includes unlimited calling and texting on Pro, at $499 a month for up to 10 users. A team that texts and calls heavily should price its own volume before assuming GoHighLevel comes out cheaper. Follow Up Boss also needs a website from another vendor, while GoHighLevel's plan includes a website builder; IDX home search is a separate bill with either.

items.q: Do I need an EIN to send texts from GoHighLevel or Follow Up Boss?
items.a:
For Follow Up Boss, yes. Its help center says the account owner needs an EIN to complete Business Registration, its name for US carrier registration, and gives Canadian businesses a route using their Business Number. One registration then covers every team member and every number added later, and Follow Up Boss covers the fees.

GoHighLevel accepts a business without a Tax ID, but HighLevel's registration guide limits that business to a single phone number. HighLevel's fee article lists the one-number Sole Proprietor tier at $22.50 once, then $2.00 a month, with a cap of 3,000 text segments a day. With an EIN, a GoHighLevel account can register a Low Volume Standard brand for the same $22.50, link several numbers and send up to 6,000 segments a day, which suits a team better.

items.q: Can GoHighLevel round-robin leads to agents on a team?
items.a:
Yes. HighLevel's Assign To User workflow action rotates new contacts among the users you choose, one after another, or splits them by weight, so one agent can receive 5 leads for every 2 that another receives. A toggle restricts it to contacts with no owner yet, which stops a returning client from being handed to a different agent.

Because the action sits inside a workflow you build, narrower rules such as routing by ZIP code or price need extra workflow steps. For complex logic, HighLevel's help article shows outside software choosing the agent and sending the choice back through an inbound webhook, a premium trigger that costs $0.01 per execution once a sub-account has used its first 100, a one-time allowance rather than a monthly one. Follow Up Boss offers round robin as a ready-made option, beside first to claim, routing by area or price, and lead ponds.

items.q: Does GoHighLevel include calling for real estate agents?
items.a:
Yes, as a metered service. HighLevel's pricing page lists inbound and outbound calling among the core features on every plan, and its phone system bills by the minute: $0.0166 for an outbound call in the US or Canada, plus a conference charge of $0.0018 a minute per participant, and $0.01165 for an inbound call answered in the browser or app, or $0.02 when forwarded to a US cell phone; partial minutes round up. Each local number costs $1.15 a month, recording adds $0.0025 a minute and transcription $0.024 a minute.

Follow Up Boss prices calling per person instead: $39 per user a month as an add-on to Grow, with calling and texting unlimited on Pro. Its calling page describes call lists, one-click dialing, automatic recording and AI call summaries. An agent who spends hours a day on the phone may find Follow Up Boss's flat price easier to budget; one who calls occasionally pays little on GoHighLevel's meter.

items.q: Is GoHighLevel good for real estate investors and wholesalers?
items.a:
For marketing to sellers, GoHighLevel fits well. An investor or wholesaler can build landing pages and funnels, track each property in a pipeline, and follow up by text and email from one account. HighLevel's pricing guide lists its Ad Manager, which creates Facebook ads and syncs the leads they bring in, with no platform fee; the ad spend itself is billed separately.

Texting at volume is the part to plan. Each segment costs $0.00747 plus a carrier fee, and the A2P tier sets a daily ceiling: 3,000 segments for a one-number registration without a Tax ID, 6,000 for a Low Volume Standard brand and 600,000 for a High Volume Standard brand, while a Low Volume Mixed campaign allows 2,000 segments a day to T-Mobile numbers. Carriers expect consent, so text owners who asked to hear from you, not purchased lists. Follow Up Boss's FAQ says its Automations send no drip texts, which leaves sequences to partner tools.

items.q: How do I move my contacts from Follow Up Boss to GoHighLevel?
items.a:
Export your data from Follow Up Boss, then import it into GoHighLevel as a CSV file. Follow Up Boss's FAQ says you own your data and can export all of it at any time. HighLevel's import guide accepts CSV files only, under 30 MB and with a single sheet, and can create contacts and opportunities in one pass when each row carries columns such as pipeline and stage.

Before importing, create custom fields in GoHighLevel for anything Follow Up Boss tracks that HighLevel lacks, because unmapped columns are ignored. Neither vendor describes a way to carry over routing rules or automations, so plan to rebuild them as HighLevel workflows. HighLevel's A2P article also says texting US mobile numbers from a local number requires registration, so register your GoHighLevel number before texting the imported contacts.
